title: Define review lattice and decision owners for scope triage on structured-output changes
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Background: Multiple PRD changes to structured output (schema enforcement, function/tool calling fields, and expanded typing) have produced unclear decision paths across Eng, Design, and Legal. Multiple teams are reviewing overlapping concerns (API contract, UX affordances, export/privacy semantics). Goal: create a single, lightweight 'review lattice' — a documented decision matrix that defines reviewers, owners, and escalation lanes for scope trade-offs and final acceptance. This should reduce PRD churn, shorten review latency, and make rollout sign-offs auditable.

Scope:
- Applies to Structured Output changes in Redwood API and Console (generation -> structured contract).
- Covers PRD scope clarifications, backward-compatibility trade-offs, telemetry/PII classification, and rollout gating.
- Does NOT cover model architecture changes or infra-only kernel switches (those follow infra review).

Out-of-scope: feature flags implementation details and pricing decisions (handled by Revenue Ops).
acceptance_criteria: A single Google doc (decision matrix) exists with explicit reviewer/approver roles per change class (minor, compatibility-breaking, telemetry-impacting).
Each role maps to a named owner with primary/secondary contacts and maximum review SLA (48h for minor, 5 business days for major).
Legal has a checklist entry for PII/Export implications and certifies path for any telemetry export changes.
Design provides required UX mockups or a clear exemption reason before final acceptance for surface-impacting items.
Eng provides an API contract PR (OpenAPI diff or schema diff) linked to the PRD; no acceptance without contract that lists fallback behavior.
A lightweight audit trail is created: PRD -> decision matrix snapshot -> sign-off record (name + timestamp).
updates: 2026-02-25: Ticket created after recurring PRD delays observed in Structured Output initiative. Initial list of stakeholders compiled (Eng: Liam O'Connor, Design: Elena Ruiz, Legal: Marco Silva).

2026-03-01: Convened kick-off (30m) with Eng/Design/Legal. Agreed to prototype decision matrix and run a pilot on next PRD for 'structured-typing 1.3'. Action: Diego to draft matrix; Elena to outline design acceptance artifacts.
2026-03-05: Draft decision matrix v0.1 created (Drive link below). Legal flagged telemetry export classification ambiguity — added 'legal pre-check' step to major-change lane.
2026-03-09: Engineering called out need for explicit API contract template. Created 'API contract minimal checklist' and assigned ENG-18492 as follow-up.
2026-03-11: Design submitted example mockups for minor vs major UX changes; agreed that minor changes may use an 'exemption note' when friction is low.

2026-03-12: Internal review with PM/Eng/Design. Next steps: finalize matrix v0.2, pilot on PRD-STR-13, and schedule sign-off cadence. Diego to gather owner confirmations and set up weekly 15m signoff slot.
